slides.headline: What makes it an operation
slides.body: Around those five commands stand six facts, each with a consequence.

rows: Other contributors must stop work during the cleanup
announce a freeze; work pushed during the rewrite is discarded or forces a restart
All refs, tags included, must be force-pushed
rules that block force pushes and tag updates must be switched off temporarily, and back on afterwards
review comments on open pull requests detach; diffs of closed ones break; every recorded ID is stale
Signatures are removed, also on commits that predate the removed data
a "require signed commits" rule now rejects the rewritten history unless bypassed
Orphaned LFS objects are not removed by the rewrite
Pull request refs, forks and other clones keep the old history

For that data, and only for that data, you want the repository's history to stop containing it.

beats.text: One. It refuses to run outside a fresh clone unless forced, because the rewrite is irreversible: by default it ends with an immediate pruning of reflogs and old objects. A reflog is a clone's own list of where each ref has pointed, and pruning means deleting.

beats.text: Two. The option --sensitive-data-removal exists since version 2.47. It fetches all refs first and gathers the extra information needed to clean up other copies.
